title: Observability agent profiles and service-health playback for Dedicated/Private
creator: Diego Morales
description: Problem: Dedicated and Private deployments currently ingest tracing/metrics/logs using a generic collector image; this leads to variable per-tenant telemetry quality, occasional cross-tenant noise during burst windows, and limited tools for playback/forensics for customer incidents. Goal: introduce deployable observability agent profiles plus a curated set of service-health playback features so SRE/SEs can reproduce latency/error spikes in a tenant-scoped way without exposing other tenants' data or increasing operator burden. Work covers collector-side (agent profile configs, tenant-scoped sampling, span id translation), control-plane (profile distribution, RBAC), and UX (service-health playback dashboard with sampled trace replay and error heatmaps).
acceptance_criteria: Agent profiles: must be selectable per-deployment and versioned; three built-in profiles (production, debug-high-sample, metrics-only) are available in the catalog
Tenant isolation: collector enforces record-level tenant scoping and drops cross-tenant spans; test harness demonstrates no cross-tenant leakage under synthetic burst
Span stitching: edge->sidecar->runtime spans maintain consistent trace/span ids via canonical translation layer; example traces from e2e tests show contiguous timelines
Playback UI: service-health view can replay sampled traces for a selected tenant and time window, and surface top error traces and 95th/99th latency histograms
Operational runbook: includes upgrade steps, rollback, and mitigation for agent misconfiguration; security sign-off documented
Performance: added CPU for collector (profile=debug-high-sample) remains within 2x of baseline in small-scale stress tests; no SLO regressions for serving path
tasks: Design agent profile schema and distribution API (OPEN RFC) - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Agent+Profiles
Implement tenant-scoped sampling & record fence in on-prem collector (PR #8345) - https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector/pull/8345
Add span-id translation layer to perimeter forwarder and sidecar shim (PR #8391)
Build frontend service-health playback prototype (dashboard + playback infra) - WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2987
E2E tests: synthetic burst/tenant-isolation test harness and trace continuity checks
Security review & threat model update (contact: sec-eng@redwood.ai)
comments: 2025-01-28 Diego Morales: Created ticket after postmortem from 2024-09 telemetry burst. Proposed solution is agent profiles + playback UI. Assigned to Aisha for implementation plan.
2025-01-30 Aisha Patel: Spike completed for profile schema. Decided to make profiles immutable once released to a deployment; distribution via control plane config map. Notes in Confluence.

2025-02-05 Marcus Chen (infra review): Raised concern about using hostNetwork for sidecar due to port namespace collisions. Recommendation: use dedicated daemonset with explicit port mappings and capability minification.

2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Implementation branch created. Initial tenant-scoped sampling implemented in collector; local tests show ~12% increase in CPU for debug-high-sample profile. Flagging for perf review.
2025-02-18 Lena Fischer (PM): UX sketch for service-health playback approved. Key ask: surface top error traces and allow narrow replay by transaction id. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-22 Security review: request for threat model. Provided draft; SecEng requested mandatory signed telemetry envelopes for Private mode. Action: add envelope signing in next PR.

2025-03-03 QA: E2E harness run against minikube cluster with 50 tenants. No cross-tenant traces observed. Some noisy spans from network proxies were dropped by fence rules; QA flagged one false-positive drop (PR #8412 to adjust heuristic).

2025-03-07 Aisha Patel: Merged tenant-scope fence PR to staging (collector PR #8345). Console playback prototype branch pushed; demo scheduled for 2025-03-10 with SREs and PM. Next: security review closeout and performance baseline run on dedicated hardware.
